title: Brake Noise Testing
seoDescription: GRAS microphones for brake noise testing: dynamometer squeal tests, wheelhouse tests and on-road measurement of brake noise on combustion and electric vehicles.

props.title: Brake Noise Testing
paragraphs: Brake noise is caused by friction-induced vibration that makes the brake system radiate sound. It disturbs owners and bystanders, hurts customer satisfaction surveys and drives warranty costs, so it is tested throughout development.
Electrification changes the picture: engine masking disappears, and regenerative braking means friction brakes are used less, which calls for new brake designs and more attention to noise.

items.title: Low frequency, 100 to 1,000 Hz
items.text: Often broadband noise, described as scraping, grinding, grunt, groan, moan or judder.

items.title: Medium to high frequency, 1 to 5 kHz
items.text: Friction-induced tonal noise, typically from coupled modes between pads and rotor. Squeal starts under specific brake pressure, rotor temperature and environment.

items.title: High-frequency tonal noise, above 5 kHz
items.text: Squeal or squeak from in-plane resonances of the brake rotor.

props.body:
- Component testing and modal analysis of brake components, especially pads and rotor, with CAE correlation
- Brake dynamometer squeal test and wheelhouse test, both with microphones
